title: Inclusion-Exclusion
quickIdea: Add the single sets, subtract the pairwise overlaps, add back the triple overlaps, and keep alternating.
remember: |A u B u C| = sum singles - sum pairs + triple.
General: |union| = sum |Ai| - sum |Ai n Aj| + sum |Ai n Aj n Ak| - ...
For 'at least one' questions, the complement is often cheaper: |U| - |union of complements|.
Divisibility questions: |A n B| counts multiples of the LCM.

example.prompt: Integers in 1..500 divisible by 3 or 5 or 7.

gateAngle: GATE CS 2017 Set 1 Q.47 (271) is the pure three-set form; GATE 2004 (IT) Q.2 (25) is the same formula read backwards to find 'none of these'.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: How many numbers in 1..1000 are divisible by 2 or 3 or 5?
variations.why: 500 + 333 + 200 - 166 - 100 - 66 + 33 = 734. Note the pairwise intersections use LCMs 6, 10, 15 and the triple uses 30.

trap.what: Stopping at the pairwise subtraction in a three-set problem.
trap.why: Elements in all three sets were added three times and subtracted three times, so they are currently missing and must be added back once.
trap.counterexample: With |A|=|B|=|C|=2 and every intersection equal to 1, the true union is 2, and 6 - 3 = 3 without the +1 term.

check.question: |A| = 10, |B| = 8, |A n B| = 3. What is |A u B|?
